claims.claim: Amazon's structural position links hyperscale compute, AI infrastructure, logistics and commerce demand; AWS converts power, chips, networking and data-center capacity into programmable infrastructure used by organizations and end users.

The present successor bottleneck is capital-efficient expansion of power/data-center/accelerator capacity: demand can remain strong while free cash flow weakens if infrastructure intensity outruns monetization.

causalEdges: AI/application demand -> AWS compute demand -> chips/power/data-center capacity -> infrastructure capex
infrastructure buildout -> service capacity -> enterprise digital/AI workloads
capex intensity -> lower near-term free cash flow -> higher required future returns
falsifiers: AI infrastructure additions fail to earn returns above their capital and operating cost.
Customers shift material workloads to competing clouds or more efficient architectures, reducing utilization/pricing leverage.
unknowns: long-run returns on current AI infrastructure investment
timing of capex-intensity and free-cash-flow normalization

claims.claim: Strong AWS and operating-income growth coexist with negative trailing free cash flow as AI infrastructure spending accelerates; this is a real capital-efficiency tension, not evidence that demand is weak.
Scale and cross-division leverage are strengths, but they can amplify capital commitments; current evidence does not establish long-run returns on the AI investment wave.

contradictions.contradiction: Strong operating-income and AWS growth coexist with negative TTM free cash flow because AI capex accelerated materially.

unknowns: long-run returns on current AI infrastructure investment
timing of capex-intensity and free-cash-flow normalization
